newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Incentive's Q1 profit falls 29 percent.
newsitem.headline: Incentive's Q1 profit falls 29 percent.

text.p: Swedish investment company Incentive AB on Monday posted a 29 percent fall in profits after financial items, saying sales growth was modest in the first quarter and many markets had levelled off.
The company said its profit after financial items slid to 828 million crowns including associates from 1.17 billion crowns in the same 1996 period.
Sales fell to 4.78 billion crowns from 5.29 billion, Incentive said in its first quarter statement.
The group's profit in its own operations fell to 473 million crowns from 826 million. The result included one-off gains of 435 million crowns compared to 570 million.

The result included charges for amortization of goodwill totalling 142 million crowns versus 73 million in the same 1996 period and increased financial expenses for the acquisition of Gambro which it purchased for 10.5 billion crowns in March 1996.

Incentive was expected to post a pre-tax profit of 921 million crowns ($117 million) in the first quarter of 1997, a Reuter poll showed. The share was trading at 512 crowns, down five, after the result was published.
"Operations during the first quarter of 1997 were characterized in many markets by levelling-off trends and more modest sales growth," Incentive said in the statement.
It said currency results were negligible as a result of hedging.

Sales in medical technology, its largest division, rose 11 percent to 2.90 billion crowns, but only eight percent adjusted for currency effects. It said the clinics it had acquired and set up during the period had so far had no any effect on sales.
But it added: "A higher volume and sales growth are expected for the rest of the year."
-- Abigail Schmelz, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1003 ($ = 7.878 Swedish Crowns)
